headline: Wisconsin Prison Inmates Raise Monarchs for Mexico Migration
meta_description: 20 inmates at a Wisconsin prison are raising and tagging monarch butterflies for their thousands-mile migration to Mexico.
summary_short: A unique program at a Wisconsin prison unites inmates in caring for monarch butterflies destined for Mexico—expanding from 60 larvae to 100 this year.
body:
Twenty inmates at a Wisconsin prison are raising and tagging monarch butterflies, contributing to the insects' extraordinary thousands-mile migration to Mexico each year.

The program has grown steadily since its launch, expanding from 60 larvae in its first year to 100 this year. By tagging the butterflies before release, participants help researchers track migration patterns and monitor the health of wild populations that face habitat loss and climate pressures.

For the inmates involved, the work offers purpose and connection to something larger than themselves. Caring for the fragile creatures—from egg to chrysalis to adult—teaches patience and responsibility while supporting conservation efforts that span continents. The program demonstrates how meaningful environmental work can happen in unexpected places, turning a correctional facility into a waystation for one of nature's most remarkable journeys.
